Science said the bumblebee cannot fly. The bumblebee never got the memo.

Kevin Trudeau tells how aeronautic scientists studied its weight, its body shape and its tiny wings and concluded it couldn't get off the ground. The bee doesn't know that, so it flies anyway.

Kevin says that when your attitude is right, facts don't count, because most of what people call facts are just opinions. He closes with Henry Ford's line: whether you think you can or think you can't, you're right.

What's one opinion you've been treating as a fact?

#ad #mindset #success #attitude

He was washing dishes, completely broke, when he wrote his goal down.

Kevin Trudeau tells the story of Bruce Lee reading Think and Grow Rich. Bruce wrote a clear mission for himself: reach a specific target by making the best martial arts movies.

Kevin says that when Bruce wrote it, he was washing dishes in San Francisco without a nickel to his name. Kevin says his team has a copy of the original writing.

What goal would you write down if nothing was holding you back?

#ad #goals #success #mindset

You don't actually want the Ferrari. Ask yourself why.

Kevin Trudeau says that when someone tells him their goal is a new Ferrari, he asks why they want it. Then he asks again, and again.

Every time, the answer ends up at the same place: how they think they'll feel sitting in that car. Kevin says it's really a feeling you don't have right now.

Once you see that, you can chase the feeling directly instead of the thing.

What feeling are you really chasing right now?
